exact_task: Represent domain SOPs as decision graphs, selectively traverse them, and restrict the valid function set while guiding an LLM agent.
runtime_or_mechanism: Natural-language pseudocode SOP compiled/represented as a decision graph; graph traversal and valid-function filtering
baselines_or_contrast: General-purpose agent baselines including ReAct/AutoGPT-style systems and domain-specific comparisons
data: Multiple domains including ALFWorld-style decision tasks, search/reasoning, code generation, data cleaning and grounded customer service
evaluation: Task success and domain benchmark metrics
occupied_claim: Decision graphs/SOP routing can guide agents and constrain tool choice.
flagship_role: Mandatory ENG-200 router/SOP control; symbolic or Prolog routing is a comparator, not novelty.

exact_task: Rename tool-schema components to match a small model's pretrained naming knowledge without retraining.
model_scale: Open SLMs including Qwen2.5-3B/7B and other small models in the primary paper
runtime_or_mechanism: PA-Tool generates schema-name candidates and selects pretraining-aligned names using peakedness
baselines_or_contrast: Original tool schemas versus PA-Tool-adapted schemas; MetaTool and RoTBench
evaluation: Tool-use accuracy and schema-misalignment errors; up to 17% improvement and 80% error reduction reported
occupied_claim: Schema/interface naming alone can materially change small-model tool selection.
flagship_role: Mandatory alternative explanation for M15/M20/M22; schema identity/naming must be matched or explicitly controlled.

exact_task: Train a small model to generate/use Prolog as an external reasoning tool.
model_scale: Qwen2.5-3B reported in the primary paper
runtime_or_mechanism: Weight-changing Prolog tool-use training plus external Prolog execution
baselines_or_contrast: Non-Prolog and training/tool-use comparisons reported in the paper
data: Logical/formal reasoning tasks in Findings ACL 2026 study
occupied_claim: Small-model plus Prolog training is established.
flagship_role: Existing mandatory ENG-202 boundary control; fixed-weight core must not claim trained Prolog novelty.

exact_task: Distill full reason-act-observe trajectories from a tool-using teacher into small students while aligning data and loss to student capacity.
runtime_or_mechanism: Minimum-NLL correct-trajectory selection plus segment-weighted supervised loss emphasizing actions/final decisions
baselines_or_contrast: Agent-distillation baselines evaluated by the paper
evaluation: Task performance; SmartAD consistently outperforms reported baselines
occupied_claim: Teacher agent trajectories can transfer tool-use and decision behavior into small-model weights.
flagship_role: Mandatory ENG-202 agent-distillation control; weight adaptation is a boundary condition, not flagship novelty.

exact_task: Select teacher-generated examples targeting weak skills and fine-tune Qwen students with skill-aware supervision.
runtime_or_mechanism: Skill-based selection from teacher corpus plus supervised fine-tuning
data: 1,000 selected examples from a 100K teacher-generated corpus; five math benchmarks
evaluation: Average benchmark gains; +1.6 points on Qwen3-4B and +1.4 on Qwen3-8B versus random SFT reported
occupied_claim: Teacher-generated data plus targeted SFT can efficiently adapt Qwen weights.
flagship_role: Mandatory ENG-202 Qwen-SFT boundary control; no novelty claim for teacher-generated SFT/LoRA/QLoRA family.

exact_task: Use both positive and negative teacher reasoning traces to adapt a small Qwen model in an offline two-stage recipe.
runtime_or_mechanism: Positive-trace SFT followed by REINFORCE-style REDI using positive and negative teacher traces
baselines_or_contrast: DPO, SimPO and other distillation objectives reported by the paper
data: 131K Open-R1 traces; mathematical reasoning benchmarks including MATH-500
evaluation: MATH-500 and other reasoning metrics; 83.1% MATH-500 reported
occupied_claim: Teacher traces can drive both supervised and reinforcement-style student weight adaptation.

exact_task: Train small Qwen-family agents for multi-step reasoning and industrial tool use using generated task/workflow data.
model_scale: Small AgenticQwen family; exact per-model sizes remain in the primary paper
runtime_or_mechanism: Multi-round reasoning RL plus agentic RL with dual synthetic/open-data flywheels; workflows expanded into multi-branch behavior trees
baselines_or_contrast: Public agentic benchmark baselines and larger-model industrial comparisons
data: Public agentic benchmarks plus industrial search/data-analysis agent system
occupied_claim: Small Qwen-family tool-use ability can be produced through synthetic workflow generation and RL.
flagship_role: Mandatory ENG-202/Qwen tool-use adaptation control; also prevents treating behavior-tree supervision as novel.

exact_task: Measure whether tool-using agents converge toward teacher-specific non-mandatory behaviors and validate that convergence with controlled distillation.
model_scale: 18 models from 8 providers in ecosystem study; controlled distillation experiment additionally reported
runtime_or_mechanism: Action Graph Similarity and Response Pattern Similarity plus controlled distillation
evaluation: AGS/RPS behavioral similarity and controlled teacher-specific convergence
occupied_claim: Distillation can produce teacher-specific tool-use/action-pattern convergence beyond task improvement.
flagship_role: ENG-202 diagnostic control: adapted-model gains and behavioral similarity must not be conflated with the fixed-weight semantic-placement mechanism.
